title: Most used tags
statement:
A blog keeps a list of every tag used on every post, with repeats. Given `tags` and a number `k`, return the `k` tags used most often, in any order.

The answer is guaranteed to be unique: there is never a tie for the kth place.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can there be a tie for the kth place?
Does the output order matter?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Lets you skip a final sort.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is k always valid?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, 1 <= k <= number of distinct tags.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How many tags?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Sorting all counts is fine; a heap or buckets can do better.

hiddenConstraints: k is at most the number of distinct tags.

edgeCases.input: k equals the number of distinct tags

edgeCases.why: Return the single most frequent tag.

approaches.name: Count, then sort by count
approaches.idea: Count with a hash map and sort the distinct tags by count descending.
approaches.tradeoffs: Simple; d is the number of distinct tags.

approaches.name: Count, then a size-k min-heap
approaches.idea: Push (count, tag) pairs, popping the smallest whenever the heap exceeds k.
approaches.tradeoffs: Better when k is much smaller than d.

approaches.name: Count, then bucket by frequency
approaches.idea: Make buckets indexed by count (at most n) and read from the highest bucket down until you have k tags.
approaches.tradeoffs: Linear; uses an array of size n + 1.

optimal.name: Hash map plus a size-k heap (or buckets)
optimal.explanation: Count each tag. Keep a min-heap of (count, tag) with at most k entries, popping the smallest when it grows past k. The heap then holds the k most frequent tags. Buckets by frequency give O(n) if needed.

hintLadder: First, how would you know how often each tag appears?
Once you have counts, do you need a full sort?
How can you keep only the best k seen so far?
Count with a hash map, then keep a min-heap of size k, or bucket tags by count.

expectedMentions.what: Asks about ties or output order
Counts with a hash map first
Proposes a size-k min-heap and states O(n + d log k)
Explains why the heap is a min-heap (to evict the smallest)
Mentions bucket sort by frequency for O(n)

followUps: Tags arrive as a stream; report the top k at any moment.

walkthrough.say: There’s never a tie for the kth spot, and the output can be in any order?
First I count each tag with a hash map, O(n). Then I need the k largest counts. Sorting all distinct tags is d log d, which is fine, but a heap of size k does d log k.
It’s a min-heap so the smallest of my current top k is on top and can be evicted when something bigger comes in. There’s also a bucket approach by frequency that gets O(n), which I can mention.
Keep at most k items, dropping the least frequent.
For go, rust, go, sql, rust, go with k of 2: counts are go 3, rust 2, sql 1. Push go and rust; pushing sql makes three, so pop the smallest, sql. Left with go and rust.
With k of 1 on x, y, y, z, y: y has 3 and every other tag gets evicted, so just y.
O(n plus d log k) time and O(d) space for the counts.
